findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the catch-up mechanism: state whether the ADR fixes full-rebuild-on-mismatch or incremental diff-based update (and reconcile the epic constraint 'full rebuild on any mismatch' with the child's `git diff --name-only` incremental rule), since this determines the AC4 cold-catch-up cost.
evidence: Epic constraint: 'catch-up happens in the reader's process on next use, keyed by the tickets-branch HEAD SHA, with full rebuild on any mismatch'
First child (roundbuilt-manlike-tapaculo) ADR scope: 'the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>)'

A full rebuild on any HEAD mismatch re-summarizes and re-embeds the entire live store (5,663+ tickets) on every tickets-branch advance, which contradicts an incremental diff-based update and drives a far larger cold-catch-up cost than AC4 anticipates
findings.finding: The epic's catch-up constraint mandates 'full rebuild on any mismatch' of the HEAD-SHA key, but the delegated ADR mechanism is incremental (`git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>`); the two are structurally different catch-up mechanisms and the plan does not reconcile which one the ADR fixes.
findings.location: Constraints every design must satisfy (bullet 2: 'catch-up happens in the reader's process ... with full rebuild on any mismatch') vs. AC1/AC4 delegation to the ADR and the first child's 'catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>)'
scenarios: Index SHA is one commit behind HEAD after a single new create: 'full rebuild' re-embeds thousands of tickets, while 'incremental' re-embeds only the changed ticket
AC4 cold-catch-up p95 measurement depends entirely on which mechanism the ADR actually fixes
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the epic's catch-up constraint to permit incremental catch-up keyed off the HEAD-SHA diff (reserving full rebuild only for a format-version bump or a non-ancestor SHA), so the constraint and the child's `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>` rule describe one mechanism.

evidence: Child: 'The returned TicketDigest JSON is committed to evals/similar-tickets/digests.json ... so the recall tables are recomputable from the committed fixture with no model access.' — stated for candidate 2 only.
Child: 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 returns AccessDeniedException there ... candidate 3 is not [entitled].' and 'recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting'.
Parent AC1: 'The measurements are reproducible from the committed benchmark spec.'
Search for 'embeddings.json' under evals/ returns no matches — no committed vector cache exists.
container pairing: parent + c670-c285-a0f9-4b40
findings.finding: Child c670 does not commit an embedding cache for candidate 3 (vector), unlike the committed digests.json that makes candidate 2 reproducible without model access. Combined with the child's own note that Titan is not entitled today (iam_s7.tf scopes bedrock:InvokeModel to anthropic.claude-* only) and candidate 3 MAY be recorded 'unavailable', the vector candidate's recall@5/@10 tables cannot be re-derived from the committed fixture. This is in tension with parent AC1's requirement that 'The measurements are reproducible from the committed benchmark spec' and the child's own AC2 check 're-running each command and matching the ADR tables'.
findings.location: child c670-c285-a0f9-4b40 Approach (candidate 3 / digest serialization) and AC2
scenarios: A reviewer re-running measure.py --candidate vector without a developer AWS identity holding Titan entitlement gets 'unavailable' and cannot reproduce the committed vector recall figures that AC1 requires to be reproducible.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the digests.json caching approach for candidate 3: commit normalized Titan vectors keyed by ticket id + SHA-256(digest_input + model id), and have the runner recompute recall from the cache on a key match with no Bedrock call.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State AC1's selection rule: the minimum recall@5/@10 on the semantic stratum (and/or the margin by which the chosen method must beat the create-time same-title journal baseline) that qualifies an architecture as the ADR choice, and quantify what 'near-saturate' means for the lexical control.
evidence: 'The architecture is justified from the semantic stratum; the lexical stratum is a control every candidate is expected to near-saturate.'
'near-saturate' is unquantified and no win-threshold or beat-the-baseline margin is stated
findings.finding: AC1 requires the ADR to justify the architecture 'from the semantic stratum' with a lexical control the candidates 'near-saturate', but states no numeric decision rule (e.g. minimum recall@5 on the semantic stratum, or the margin by which the chosen method must beat the AC2 same-title journal baseline). An executor measuring recall@5=0.4 cannot tell from the plan whether that is a pass.
scenarios: Research child measures several architectures and must pick one, but no stated bar defines 'good enough' or the required improvement over the repurposed create-time journal baseline named in Context.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per arm, the failure disposition of the advisory similar-tickets field: when the embedding/semantic catch-up fails (model error, index mismatch, or rebuild timeout), does `create` surface lexical-tier results or an empty advisory, and is that degradation non-fatal (advisory never blocks create)? Record which tier wins when the semantic path is unavailable so a transient embedding failure is not surfaced as authoritative emptiness.
evidence: 'whether catch-up embeds the backlog synchronously inside that next create or serves it from the lexical tier until the next batch step'
'Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking, capped ... and gated on a minimum title length' — non-blocking implies degradation but the degraded disposition is unstated
'its event write never spawns, queues, or waits on indexing' fixes the WRITE disposition but not the advisory-read disposition on embedding/index failure
ABSENCE: no explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) for the embedding or catch-up arm
findings.finding: The plan introduces a degradation path — compose-time suggestion 'serves it from the lexical tier until the next batch step' and read-phase catch-up that MAY embed synchronously — but never states the failure disposition of the advisory field when the semantic/embedding path itself fails (model call error, index build failure, or HEAD-SHA mismatch mid-catch-up). What does `create` surface in the `similar` field then: an empty list, lexical-only results, or a surfaced error?
scenarios: Embedding model call fails during a cold-catch-up create
Index rebuild cannot complete within the read phase (HEAD SHA mismatch, large backlog)
Vector store unavailable while lexical tier is available
findings.suggested_fix: In the Constraints or AC4, add a one-line disposition contract: the advisory field is best-effort/non-fatal — a failed or incomplete semantic catch-up degrades to lexical-tier results (never an error, never blocks the write), and the degradation is reported (e.g., a tier/source flag in the advisory output) so callers can tell semantic coverage is cold. Defer the measured cost to the ADR but fix the disposition here.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the Research/design child (AC1) explicitly verify and record the chosen embedding SURFACE — provider, endpoint/model id, auth mechanism (API key vs. Bedrock IAM), HTTPS precondition, and rate limits — classifying it MATCH/MISMATCH/UNVERIFIED against the current pydantic-ai provider seam before the ADR commits to it.
evidence: Plan: 'This is a vector search problem over summaries of large tickets.' and AC1 requires the ADR to record 'embedding model and store'

Repo evidence: src/rebar/llm has no embedding model class (search for 'embed'/'vector'/'voyage' in src/rebar returns no embedding/vector-store code); ADR 0086 is titled '...no embeddings' and chose Cupid digests over embeddings — so this is a NEW external capability, not an already-used one

Evidence class = Unverified: Anthropic exposes no first-party embeddings API, so the embedding surface (vendor, endpoint, auth scope, HTTPS precondition) is unconfirmed and depends on the research child's choice

The plan does route this through a SPIKE-equivalent (first child writes the ADR before implementation children are created), which satisfies the 'route a capability gap to a SPIKE' check — the gap is only that the surface-existence/auth verification is not named as an explicit output of that child
findings.finding: The plan commits to embeddings + a vector store as the retrieval mechanism but names no concrete embedding provider/model or vector store, and does not require the research/ADR child to verify that the chosen embedding SURFACE exists and is reachable (auth/HTTPS, rate limits) within rebar's existing provider seam — which today is Anthropic/Bedrock chat-only with no embedding endpoint used anywhere.
findings.location: AC1 (ADR records 'embedding model and store') and 'Constraints every design must satisfy' / 'Child decomposition' (first child: Research and design)
scenarios: The ADR child selects an embedding provider whose endpoint/auth cannot be reached through rebar's pydantic-ai provider seam, forcing a re-architecture after the design appears to have landed
Implementation children (criteria 2–4) are spun up against an embedding surface whose rate limits or auth (API key vs. Bedrock IAM) were never verified, causing silent runtime failure after ship
findings.suggested_fix: In AC1's checklist and the first child's scope, add that the ADR must name the concrete embedding provider/model and vector store AND include a reachability/auth check (e.g. a minimal embed call succeeding through rebar's provider seam, with the auth mechanism and HTTPS precondition stated), so a capability gap is caught inside the research spike rather than in the implementation children.
